ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Lili Boulanger Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for four months of abdominal pain, diarrhea, fevers, and weight loss. Concerns: Four months of cramping pain low on the right of the abdomen, loose stools up to six times a day and at night, evening fevers, and weight loss; Has been unwell, on and off, since childhood and wants a clear answer and a plan that lets her keep composing and performing. [S]

tr.td: Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, one or two tablets by mouth up to every 6 hours as needed for abdominal pain, no more than 3000 mg a day; no nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
One or two tablets up to every 6 hours as needed
Prednisone 20 mg oral tablet: 40 mg by mouth each morning, reduced by 5 mg each week over eight weeks, as a bridge until risankizumab takes effect
40 mg each morning, tapering by 5 mg weekly
Risankizumab 600 mg in 10 mL intravenous infusion over at least one hour at weeks 0, 4, and 8 (induction)
One infusion every 4 weeks for three doses
Risankizumab 360 mg in 2.4 mL by subcutaneous on-body injector every 8 weeks (maintenance), from week 12
Ferric derisomaltose 1000 mg in 10 mL intravenous infusion, single dose
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 1889 units oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily
Calcium carbonate 1250 mg (500 mg elemental calcium) oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily with food while on prednisone

tr.td: Chest X-ray before possible immunosuppression and to look for tuberculosis: normal lungs, no hilar nodes, no calcified granulomas

Ileocolonoscopy with biopsies: deep longitudinal ulcers over the last 15 cm of the terminal ileum; patchy aphthous and serpiginous ulcers in the ascending and transverse colon with normal mucosa between; rectum spared; ileocecal valve patulous, not stenosed; SES-CD 14. Biopsies: chronic active ileitis and colitis with crypt architectural distortion and a few small non-caseating granulomas; acid-fast stain negative, TB PCR (Xpert MTB/RIF) negative; mycobacterial culture sent

MR enterography: 18 cm of terminal ileal wall thickening (7 mm) with mucosal hyperenhancement and the comb sign; no stricture with upstream dilation, no fistula, abscess, or necrotic lymph nodes; no ascites; ascending colon wall thickening
Baseline bone density scan (DXA): lumbar spine Z-score -1.4, femoral neck Z-score -1.1, within the expected range for age
Follow-up ileocolonoscopy eight months into risankizumab: healed ileal ulcers with a few small aphthae and scarring; colon healed; SES-CD 2 (endoscopic response, near remission); no stricture

list.item: Crohn disease of the terminal ileum and colon (ileocolitis), Montreal A2 L3 B1 without perianal disease, moderate to severe: deep ileal ulcers over 15 cm and patchy colonic ulcers, SES-CD 14, Harvey-Bradshaw Index 11; intestinal tuberculosis excluded by negative interferon-gamma release assay, normal chest X-ray, and biopsies negative for acid-fast bacilli, TB PCR, and mycobacterial culture; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented chronic intestinal illness, whose historical diagnosis is not settled: active, confirmed [S]

Four months of crampy right lower abdominal pain, loose stools up to six times a day including at night, low-grade evening fevers, and loss of 6 kg; inflammatory markers raised; colonoscopy and small-bowel imaging booked: resolved, confirmed [S]
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic intestinal blood loss and poor absorption (hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, MCV 76, ferritin 9): resolved, confirmed [S]
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6 after losing 6 kg (12 percent of body weight) in four months; albumin 3.3 g/dL: resolved, confirmed [S]
Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D 18 ng/mL): resolved, confirmed [S]
Long-term use of risankizumab, an immunosuppressive biologic, for Crohn disease: active, confirmed [S]

Acute norovirus gastroenteritis on risankizumab, with mild dehydration; distinguished from a Crohn flare by the sudden onset, household contacts, and a positive stool PCR; resolved in three days: resolved, confirmed [S]

Diagnosis of Crohn disease with intestinal tuberculosis excluded; inflammatory bowel disease consultation the same day
Review at week 4 of risankizumab, on the day of the second induction infusion
Review at week 12, the first maintenance dose of risankizumab
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea on risankizumab

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Workup for suspected inflammatory bowel disease: blood count, CRP, albumin, iron studies, vitamin B12 and D, fecal calprotectin, stool tests for Clostridioides difficile and enteric pathogens, celiac serology, a pregnancy test, ileocolonoscopy with biopsies, and MR enterography

Exclude intestinal tuberculosis before any steroid or immunosuppressive drug: interferon-gamma release assay, chest X-ray, and ileal and colonic biopsies for acid-fast stain, TB PCR, and mycobacterial culture; with hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, measles, and varicella serology before treatment
Gastroenterology (inflammatory bowel disease) consultation once the endoscopy and imaging are done, to confirm the diagnosis and choose treatment with her
Nutrition: dietitian assessment, small frequent meals with oral nutritional supplements, and weight at every visit
Mood, anxiety, and work: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intervals, IBD psychology if needed, and a practical plan for composing and performing during treatment

Risankizumab 600 mg intravenously at weeks 0, 4, and 8, then 360 mg subcutaneously every 8 weeks, chosen with her as early advanced therapy; liver enzymes and bilirubin at baseline and through at least week 12; a short prednisone bridge tapered over eight weeks; no live vaccines

Vaccines before immunosuppression: PCV20, recombinant zoster vaccine in two doses, a hepatitis B booster with an antibody check one to two months later, and influenza and COVID-19 vaccines each season; live vaccines not needed because she is immune to measles and varicella
Iron, vitamin D, and bone: one intravenous ferric derisomaltose infusion, vitamin D3 daily, calcium while on prednisone, baseline DXA, and weight-bearing exercise
Treat to target: symptoms and CRP at every visit, fecal calprotectin at about three and six months, and ileocolonoscopy at six to twelve months

Contraception, fertility, and pregnancy planning: effective contraception while the disease is active; plan pregnancy after three to six months of steroid-free remission, with a preconception review; continue the biologic in pregnancy after discussing the limited data for risankizumab; folic acid before conception
Reach a diagnosis, with tuberculosis excluded, within two weeks

Ileocolonoscopy, biopsies, MR enterography, interferon-gamma release assay, and chest X-ray completed in nine days; Crohn disease diagnosed and intestinal tuberculosis made very unlikely, with the mycobacterial culture still pending
Steroid-free clinical remission by week 12 to 16 of treatment
Harvey-Bradshaw Index 2 at week 12, five weeks after the prednisone taper ended
Normal CRP and fecal calprotectin by six months, and endoscopic response at six to twelve months
CRP 2 mg/L and calprotectin 42 ug/g at six months; SES-CD 14 to 2 at eight months
Regain weight to a BMI of 19 or more and correct iron and vitamin D
Weight 50.6 kg (BMI 19.8); hemoglobin 13.1, ferritin 72, vitamin D 34
Perform her March concert and keep composing through treatment
Composing most mornings; the concert went ahead in late March with a plan for bathroom access
